plan: In a second-price sealed bid auction with independent values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Since my private value is $39, bidding exactly $39 maximizes my expected profit. This ensures I win if my value is highest, and I'll only pay the second-highest bid. Bidding less risks losing the item, while bidding more doesn't improve my potential outcome. With no prior round history, a true-value bid is optimal.

With a private value of $20, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since the auction pays the second-highest bid, I want to bid strategically. With three bidders and values randomly drawn between $0-$49, a bid around my true value makes sense. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk losing money if I win. A bid of $22-$25 seems optimal - high enough to potentially win, but not overcommitting.

My private value is $20. In a second-price sealed bid auction, optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn and this is a single round, I'll bid exactly my private value of $20, which maximizes my expected profit.
